 L.A. Weekend Guide: Benny Boy Brewery Applefest, Camp Flog Gnaw, CicLAvia Pasadena
 Plus, Black Beauty Block Party and Yappy Hour at 33 Taps
 Lauren Durham 
 • Nov 12, 2026 
 Add as a preferred source on Google 
 Benny Boy Brewery Credit: Kat Hanegraaf 
 Every Thursday,  Los Angeles  magazine  curates a list of the best events in and around Los Angeles. Craft a great last-minute schedule with our  Weekend Guide  to L.A., and don’t forget to sign up to have the guide delivered to your inbox every week by clicking  HERE .
 A Sense of Home Gala LA — Nov. 12  
 Members of Change Reaction attend A Sense of Home Gala Presented by Jenni Kayne, Voluspa, and Ruggable at Pacific Design Center on October 04, 2025 in West Hollywood, California. Credit: (Photo by Stefanie Keenan/Getty Images for A Sense of Home) 
 Hosted by Karen Pittman, the Legacy of Home Gala will celebrate founders Georgie Smith and Melissa Goddard as they relinquish themselves from the company’s daily responsibilities. The evening focuses on raising funds to support young adults aging out of Los Angeles’ foster care system, providing a place to call home and a community of support to aid in their transition into adulthood. Drew Scott of HGTV’s Property Brothers and Regina Brodell are also set to be honored with the first-ever Founders Award.
 Peacock’s DIG x Go Greek Yogurt — Nov. 13-22  
 Credit: Go Greek Yogurt 
 Much like the show’s talented team of architects, Go Greek Yogurt encourages customers to dig into its new DIG Discovery Bowl. Available for a limited time leading up to the series premiere on Nov. 23, the bowl features cookie crumbles, blueberries and a honey drizzle, all layered with the tart base of Greek frozen yogurt.
 Applefest at Benny Boy Brewing — Nov. 14-15  
 Credit: Kat Hanegraaf 
 This fall festival brings apple orchard fun to the Lincoln Heights brewery with seasonal bites, beverages, activities and live music. Most notably, the community crush allows volunteers to press apples the old-fashioned way, resulting in a craft cider for attendees to enjoy. Food vendors including Gochu Gang, Xijuana Tacos and Shourai BBQ complement cider flights ranging from traditional to modern flavors.

 Camp Flog Gnaw — Nov. 14-15  
 Credit: (Photo by Rich Fury/Getty Images) 
 Tyler, the Creator’s annual festival takes over the Dodger Stadium parkling lot for a weekend of nonstop musical prowess. Headliners for this year include the founder, Don Toliver, Steve Lacy, Future and Turnstile, with 38 additional supporting acts taking the stage throughout. 
 Eli Brown @ City Market Downtown Los Angeles – Nov. 14  
 Eli Brown performs at Electric Forest Music Festival in Rothbury, Michigan on June 25, 2026. Credit: ALIVE for Electric Forest 
 The British DJ makes his mark on Los Angeles immediately following the release of his debut album, Panic Attack . The high-energy house and electronic music at this warehouse release celebration create the perfect backdrop to sweat it all out on the dance floor.
 Inglewood Open Studios Art Walk — Nov. 14-15  
 Credit: John Gaylord 
 The free, self-guided art walk at Inglewood Open Studios returns after a year-long hiatus. Highlighting local artists, the 2026 Art Walk marks the 20th anniversary of the inaugural event, now with a redesigned website that allows guests to curate their own personalized itinerary and map. 
 Live on Sunset — Nov. 14  
 Credit: Jon Viscott 
 Sunset Boulevard is shut down from San Vincente to Doheny Boulevard for a free concert throughout Saturday, headlined by Sheryl Crow and supported by Local Natives, Empress Of, Grace Bowers, Doug Locke and Mia Moretti. The event offers a free shuttle from nearby parking locations and features local food and goods vendors, such as Dialog Cafe, Prince Street Pizza and Out of Date Records.
 ModA Gala 2026 — Nov. 14  
 View this post on Instagram A post shared by Modern Anthropology (@house_modastudio) 
 Hosting its first annual charity gala, the nonprofit Modern Anthropology Studios aims to promote an understanding of contemporary culture through the exploration of interdisciplinary art. The evening includes a silent art auction, as well as the fall exhibition, Life in the Objects We Don’t Know , which examines how physical art can hold history, culture and identity. The exhibit features seven different artists from a range of cultural and ethnic backgrounds, including Chinese, Palestinian, Austrian and Korean influences. 
 NoHo’s Berman Ceramic Arts Annual Holiday Sale — Nov. 14-15  
 Credit: Jennifer Sax 
 L.A.’s longest running independent ceramic studio hosts its annual holiday sale, featuring hand-crafted items from 56 Angeleno artists. Established in 1972, founder Harry Berman will be present both days to welcome and chat with guests as they wander the gallery and enjoy free bites and treats.
 33 Taps x Vanderpump Dogs Yappy Hour — Nov. 14  
 Credit: Cara Harman 
 Pet care brand Cleo&Hooman team up with pup-fluencer @ford_explores for a Yappy Hour benefit event benefiting The Vanderpump Dog Foundation. Come together with a furry friend to enjoy the 33 Taps West Hollywood’s puppy menu and cocktails specially curated for both humans and pets. Additionally, Cleo&Hooman’s pet care essentials will be available for browsing.
 Black Beauty Block Party — Nov. 15  
 Credit: Jorge Meza 
 The fourth annual Black Beauty Block Party visits The Preserve L.A. for a day of celebrating Black beauty, culture and local Los Angeles entrepreneurship. Live shopping opportunities, giveaways and DJ sets are open to wander, while panels give guests opportunities to chat with special guests Angela Simmons and Amanda Scott.
 CicLAvia Pasadena — Nov. 15  
 Credit: CicLAvia Los Angeles 
 CicLAvia partners with the city of Pasadena to create a 2.7-mile stretch of car-free zones for community members to experience their city in a new way. Whether walking, skating or cycling, CicLAvia provides hubs with family-friendly activities, free bike repair and water stations that encourage attendees to slow down and find meaningful connection with their community.
 ¡HOLA ALTA! — Nov. 15  
 Credit: Arlene Mejorado 
 This free community event celebrates the public launch of a new arts and culture space by AltaMed Health Services, The Alta. Chicana artist Patssi Valdez presents her first solo exhibit in over a decade as the inaugural program of the new opening. Other highlights of the day include live performances, food vendors and family friendly interactive options, such as a butterfly garden and a scavenger hunt.
 Oaxacan Recipes and Remembrance with Bricia Lopez at Getty Center — Nov. 15  
 Credit: Cassia Davis © 2022 J. Paul Getty Trust 
 Renowned chef, author and Guelaguetza co-owner Bricia Lopez shares how food connects culture and memories across history in her personal lecture featuring familial traditions and Oaxacan cuisine. After the chat, guests are invited to sample Oaxacan dishes and mezcals. 
 Huron Station Playhouse Presents: LUNGS — Through Nov. 29  
 Credit: Courtesy Huron Station Playhouse 
 Tony-winner Alden Ehrenreich launches the inaugural season of his new L.A. playhouse — built inside a historic trolley station — with a production of LUNGS. Starring Zoe Lister-Jones and Ashley Zukerman, this marks the first step of Ehrenreich’s goal to help transform Los Angeles into a live theatrical hub.
